record.paper_title: Open problems in the theory of completely positive and copositive matrices
record.original_question: Determine an exact formula for p_n = max{cpr(A) : A is in CP_n}, where CP_n is the cone of real symmetric n x n matrices A = B B^T with B entrywise nonnegative and cpr(A) is the minimum possible number of columns of such a nonnegative factor B.

evidence.quote: Determining an exact formula for pn is still an open problem

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer $n\ge 1$, let $\mathcal{CP}_n$ denote the cone of real symmetric $n\times n$ matrices $A$ admitting a factorization $A = BB^{T}$ with $B$ an entrywise nonnegative real matrix (with an arbitrary number of columns). For $A \in \mathcal{CP}_n$, define the cp-rank
$$\operatorname{cpr}(A) = \min\{k \in \mathbb{N} : A = BB^{T} \text{ for some entrywise nonnegative } B \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times k}\}.$$
Define
$$p_n = \max\{\operatorname{cpr}(A) : A \in \mathcal{CP}_n\}.$$
Determine an exact closed-form formula for $p_n$ as a function of $n$.
artifact.status_search_result: Only bounds for $p_n$ are known for $n\ge 6$. The Drew–Johnson–Loewy conjecture $p_n=\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor$ was disproved (Bomze–Schachinger–Ullrich and subsequent work showed higher cp-ranks are possible for $n\ge 7$). Current best upper and lower bounds leave a gap, and no exact formula has been established.

status_evidence.title: From seven to eleven: Completely positive matrices with high cp-rank
status_evidence.snippet: Examples showing cp-rank exceeds the Drew–Johnson–Loewy bound floor(n^2/4) for n between 7 and 11.
status_evidence.claim: The conjectured exact formula floor(n^2/4) for p_n fails, and only bounds are known.

status_evidence.title: Lower bounds for maximal cp-ranks of completely positive matrices and tensors
status_evidence.snippet: Improved lower bounds on the maximal cp-rank p_n.
status_evidence.claim: Research continues to focus on bounds rather than an exact formula, indicating the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: New results on the cp rank and related properties of completely positive matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds and structural results on the cp-rank.
status_evidence.claim: No exact formula for p_n is given; the maximum cp-rank remains an open problem for general n.
